description:
## Goal

Make semantic activation analysis change-proportional at the earliest incorrect cell boundary exposed by the generic scheduler telemetry in fz-kdt.34. Do not batch analyses into rounds or introduce an activation-cone pass.

## Fresh signal (release compiler, 2026-08-24)

enum_take_drop_split:

- 1,382 AnalyzeActivation evaluations, 276.120 ms;
- 237 unique materialized backend activation keys;
- 186 rebased completions, 300 blocked completions, 153 completions with no changed output fact.

fz_f98_range_map_converges:

- 307 AnalyzeActivation evaluations, 21.677 ms;
- 59 unique materialized backend activation keys;
- 27 rebased completions, 77 blocked completions, 39 completions with no changed output fact.

The unique backend inventory is not the exact analyzed-activation inventory; fz-kdt.34 must expose that distinction directly. The earlier 73 SeedActivation denominator is not a sound unique-activation count and must not guide a fix.

## Strategy

1. Use fz-kdt.34 telemetry to attribute every evaluation to exact moved input revisions.
2. Find the earliest cell whose revision changes without semantic content movement, or the formula whose dependency set is broader than the output decision it computes.
3. Repair that store/key/equivalence/dependency boundary so equivalent evidence cannot wake work.
4. If AnalyzeActivation is one formula combining independently moving decisions, split ownership at those decisions rather than adding cross-round coalescing or a cone scheduler.
5. Delete the obsolete combined path, duplicate projection, or overly broad subscription the corrected model replaces.

A necessary recalculation that observes changed input and produces unchanged output is not automatically a bug; it becomes avoidable only if the formula can truthfully own a narrower dependency set. Prove that boundary before changing it.

## Acceptance

- Every non-initial AnalyzeActivation evaluation is attributable to an exact dependency revision not previously observed.
- Semantically equivalent input movement does not revise the cell and performs no analysis.
- An unchanged output wakes no downstream work.
- Per-activation evaluation counts are bounded by the actual distinct input revisions they consume, with scheduler coalescing allowed to make the count smaller.
- Repeated runs produce identical work histograms.
- enum_take_drop_split and fz_f98_range_map_converges remain byte-correct on interp, run, and build.
- Work-count regression tests use production telemetry; no wall-clock thresholds.
- No fixture-specific Enum rule and no downstream transport/native workaround.

## Documentation

Record the corrected semantic cell boundary and remove descriptions of any combined concept or broad subscription that no longer exists.

comments.text:
FOLDED FROM THREE TICKETS. fz-f98.5 ('telemetry-first convergence audit'), fz-f98.14 ('convergence runaway: drive is 1.3s') and fz-bfh.6 ('demand/analysis re-derivation volume, ~1.8k') were evaluated independently by three different agents, and all three arrived at the same measurement on the same fixture: 1382 AnalyzeActivation spans out of 2593 job spans on enum_take_drop_split.

They differed only in what they blamed, and each blame was stale in its own way: f98.5 blamed a schedule-dependent Seal<->DeriveRuntimeDemand<->Transport cycle (all those job kinds now grep to zero); f98.14 blamed SealSemanticClosure's monolithic reseal (deleted); bfh.6 paired AnalyzeActivation with DeriveRuntimeDemand re-derivation (runtime demand is now a pull product that settles 3 times per drive, not 1.8k).

Per [[feedback_fold_concordant_ideas]] they are one ticket. Keeping three would have had three people measure the same number and re-derive three dead diagnoses.

title: Make activation analysis change-proportional at exact semantic cell boundaries
